I suppose we could, but I'd rather not have to duplicate the logic that galaxy uses to determine the validity of a collection.

I overlooked something important in the semver spec:

> Build metadata MUST be ignored when determining version precedence. Thus two versions that differ only in the build metadata, have the same precedence.

I had errantly added support to use build metadata for determining version precedence. This will be remediated shortly.

Talking with people, I think what we want to add is the ability to pass --pre-release flag to ansible-galaxy, to have galaxy client return the latest version uploaded.  This would work much like pip

For background and clarity, for the 2.9 release, we decided to not tackle this problem.  Largely this is due to collections using semver (semver allows for pre-release versioning), and to keep from introducing another dependency, we handle release versions using `distutils.version.StrictVersion`, and reject all versions that do not adhere to `StrictVersion` (pre-releases are included in this).

As a result we have no way to sort pre-releases.  Potentially we could switch to `LooseVersion` if `--pre` is specified.
thanks for info! Yah, I think LooseVersion on --pre makes sense to me.

I would suggest we look to another project, for example openstack, which has a good solution to this for python packages. They use version logic with in pbr (https://opendev.org/openstack/pbr/) for semantic versioning, I suspect we can leverage a lot of that logic if needed. 

How that falls into 1,2 or 3 would still need to be decided.

FWIW: We are using pbr today to generate our semantic versioning numbers, works well.

That would be option 3 as per https://opendev.org/openstack/pbr/src/branch/master/pbr/version.py. It remains to be seen if the ability to sort pre-release versions instead of an explicit opt in is what we want to have.

I found this ticket from https://github.com/ansible/galaxy/issues/2137

@jborean93 wrote above:
> Implement our own semantic versioning parser

On first glance, I don't think this would be impossible, particularly if we use the code from python-semanticversion as inspiration. Here's the important regular expression (from [semantic_version/base.py](https://github.com/rbarrois/python-semanticversion/blob/da55cf15dd71a0d9a839e7507e4fc69396c8326d/semantic_version/base.py#L81))

```python
version_re = re.compile(r'^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:-([0-9a-zA-Z.-]+))?(?:\+([0-9a-zA-Z.-]+))?$')
```

We could build a really small `SemanticVersion` class that implements just enough of the features we need on the client. I have posted a work-in-progress patch at https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/65676 that does this for my own use-case.

Informational:

Currently the galaxy server will show the prereleases on the galaxy UI despite /usr/bin/ansible-galaxy not serving those releases.

review_comments: I'm pretty sure this test with floats and integers instead of strings was testing to make sure `MANIFEST.json` with those values instead of a string didn't traceback ansible-galaxy like it did before a commit that fixed it. While `ansible-galaxy collection build` would never create a MANIFEST like that I can't guarantee other build tools would be the same.

I'll have to look at the code flow, but when I swapped out `LooseVersion` for `SemanticVersion`, this test began failing.

Maybe I was overzealous in my replacement.

This is due to the change at https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/68258/files#diff-2de3c8cc3e7fae814d02b3058f0c8f9eR365

That ensures that we can compare the version later with a `SemanticVersion`, so it either needs to stay, and cause us to fall back to `*`, or we would need to do what we do with user requirements:

```
SemanticVersion.from_loose_version(LooseVersion(version))
```

`from_loose_version` takes a simplified version, and attempts to convert it to a `SemanticVersion`.
